A1.justification: Both complete, readable 23-page PDFs describe the same SubPOP research, with matching main sections, Appendices A-E, equations, tables and figures. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons, generalization results, scaling analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including benchmark, subgroup and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same subpopulation/question inputs, option-probability prediction, LoRA adaptation and forward KL training objective. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain ATP-based SubPOP-Train, OpinionQA and GSS-based SubPOP-Eval, with the same survey topics, seen and unseen US subpopulations, and cross-survey generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain zero-shot QA/BIO/PORTRAY prompting, few-shot prompting and Modular Pluralism. The appendix comparisons also retain the same one-hot, response-augmentation and base/chat model alternatives.

E3.justification: The four main model configurations, Wasserstein-distance evaluation, five-example few-shot baseline and training-data fractions are unchanged. The loss comparison also retains its 90/10 OpinionQA training/validation split.

E4.justification: Both retain dataset scaling, KL-versus-WD loss comparisons, response-distribution modeling ablations, base-versus-chat analysis and subgroup-steerability heatmaps. No supplementary analysis is added, removed or substantively revised.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains 1,000 respondent-level bootstrap resamples and 95% confidence intervals for the human lower bound, also displayed in Figure 3. Repeated-run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains Llama-2-7B SubPOP-FT Wasserstein distances of 0.106 on OpinionQA and 0.121 on SubPOP-Eval; ablation, scaling and subgroup results also match.

T1.justification: The distributional objective, Wasserstein-distance formulas, intergroup-disagreement definition and weighted-bootstrap equations are mathematically unchanged. Differences in equation spacing do not revise definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the scaled SubPOP dataset, the claimed 32-46% Wasserstein-distance reduction, and generalization to unseen topics, survey families and subpopulations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of subgroup gains, steerability and scaling are retained. Both include Figure 12's qualification about the heterogeneous Other race/ethnicity group and the conclusion's open questions about intersecting identities and changing opinions.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same curation instructions, hyperparameters, 80GB A100 hardware, vLLM 0.7.2 and baseline prompts. The stated code-access link is unchanged; no reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prompting, community-based fine-tuning, survey-based methods and pluralistic alignment are unchanged. Bibliographic spacing and page flow do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: Several cross-references change from Appendix to Section, such as references to B, D and C.2, and the arXiv version header is updated. The prose, section ordering and scientific narrative otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-16 and Tables 1-10 retain their content and structure. Limited text reflow changes heading and paragraph placement: Section 4.3 begins on page 6 instead of page 7, and the conclusion finishes on page 9 instead of continuing onto page 10.

improvement.justification: The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information are retained, including the appendices. Changes to cross-reference wording, the version header and page flow do not materially improve or diminish clarity, rigor or evidential support.
